paragraphs.text: Chrome sidebar extension that lets DeepSeek Harness operate your browser directly, no vision capabil
ities required. 一款 Chrome 侧边栏扩展程序，可让 DeepSeek Harness 直接操控您的浏览器，无需视觉能力。
# dsh Browser Control
**English** | 中文

> [!NOTE]
> This is the **graydovee fork** of Lum1104/dsh-browser, keeping the upstream code and its
MIT licence. It adds what only this fork ships: permission, model, and `/`-command controls in the
side panel, an opt-in developer-tools group, viewport screenshots, and image attachments in the pane

l.
> This fork also tracks the current DSH plugin interfaces: the bridge declares `engines.dsh: ^0.2
.1-rc.2` and is verified against dsh 0.2.1-rc.3 (0.2.1-rc.2 exposes the same plugin interfaces, so i

t stays supported).
> Fork changes are recorded in CHANGELOG.md with its Chinese edition. Upstream p
ublishes no changelog, so compare the upstream side against its commit history or its tags.
Connect DeepSeek Harness to the Chrome or Firefox tabs you are already using. The model can read pag
e content, operate controls, navigate, and manage tabs while preserving your login state, session, a
nd cookies. A side panel or sidebar provides the conversation UI.
`dsh` is DeepSeek AI's open-source, plugin-based agent harness. This repository provides a companion
browser bridge plugin and Chrome/Firefox MV3 extension as one standalone pnpm workspace.
Browser operation remains text-only: pages become structured text with a numbered inventory of inter
active elements, and the model addresses those elements by number. dsh 0.2 multimodal chat is separa
te from that page channel—the side panel accepts PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF attachments when the host
advertises image support, while browser tools still never capture screenshots.

> [!IMPORTANT]
[该节后续省略]
## Quick install
[该节后续省略]
## Performance
[该节后续省略]
## Core capabilities
| Capability | Tool | Notes |
| Read page | `browser_snapshot` | Structured text snapshot: title, URL, main text, numbered control
s, and masked form fields; `delta: true` returns only changes, `frame` reads one iframe, and `query`

locates any element by text/selector/role with its selector and rect |
| Pointer | `browser_click`
| Click, double-click, hover, press, release, or drag by index or selector; canvas targets without a

n identity accept frame-local `point` coordinates |
| Text | `browser_type` | React/Vue-compatible i
nput; `replace` clears the field first, and `mode` selects caret insertion or per-character key even

ts |
| Press keys | `browser_press` | Single keys or chords (`modifiers`); `action: down/up` holds a

key across calls and `repeat` repeats it |
| Scroll | `browser_scroll` | Viewport/container scrolli

ng; with `point` it sends a real wheel gesture at those coordinates (canvas zoom/pan) |
| Clipboard
| `browser_clipboard` | `write` puts text/HTML on the system clipboard; `paste` delivers it as a pas

te event or a real platform shortcut |
| Files | `browser_upload` | Attach local files to an `input[

type=file]` (Chrome) |
| Navigate | `browser_navigate` / `browser_open_tab` / `browser_open_window`
/ `browser_back` / `browser_forward` / `browser_reload` | Navigation inside the controlled tab, open
a URL in a new tab (`active:false` keeps the current tab in front), or open a new browser window (`

focused:false` opens without stealing focus) |
| List tabs | `browser_list_tabs` | List accessible t

abs with stable IDs, titles, URLs, window/index metadata, and active/controlled state |
| Follow tab
| `browser_follow_tab` | Bind later browser tools to a tab returned by `browser_list_tabs`; it stay

s in the background unless `activate: true` |
| Close tab | `browser_close_tab` | Close a tab return

ed by `browser_list_tabs` |
| Read region | `browser_get_text` | Lazy-loaded or partial page text |

| Wait for stability | `browser_wait` | Page-load and render-settle detection |
| Send images | `ses
sion.prompt` / `session.attachment` | Host-capability-gated image drafts, image-only prompts, and du

rable history previews |
[该节后续省略]
## Why this design
- **Your real browser, not a headless copy**: the model works in the page you already have open, ret

aining logins, sessions, and cookies.
[该节后续省略]
## Security
- The bridge path sits outside the `/api` trust boundary and performs its own bearer-token authentic

ation.
- Zero-config loopback access is pinned to this extension's stable id (derived from the publi
c manifest `key`); unlisted extensions must present the bearer token. The key is public, so the pin
stops *incidental* cross-extension access — an extension deliberately copying the key inherits the i
d. Deployments that must resist hostile extensions should set `trustedExtensionOrigins: []` and pair

the bearer token. Firefox origins are per-install UUIDs and always present the token.
- The exempti
on is loopback-only. A reverse proxy terminating on 127.0.0.1 (`tailscale serve`, `ssh -L`, nginx) m

akes proxied clients appear as loopback — use the hardened mode above for such deployments.
- Privil
eged gateway methods such as `settings.*`, `credentials.*`, and `host.open*` reject non-loopback sou

rces.
- The browser-page pipeline is text-only and never captures screenshots; explicitly attached c
hat images use dsh's durable attachment service. Password and payment-card values never leave the pa

ge.
- When work begins, the assistant binds to the active tab (at prompt submission, or at the first
direct browser-tool call). If you switch tabs manually, later browser actions pause and the side pa
nel asks whether the assistant should stay on the original page or follow the current one, and offer
s "jump back to the assistant page" to move your own tab back to the assistant's page. Choosing the
original page permits background operation; apart from that button the extension never silently reta
rgets or changes your visible tab. Closing the controlled tab also pauses tools until you explicitly

select the current page.
- Text you highlight is captured only while a side panel is open and page
sharing is not `off`, and never from password or payment-card fields. It stays inside the extension
until you send the message, is dropped when you dismiss it or its page navigates or closes, and reac
hes the model inside the same untrusted-content boundary as page snapshots — including its source ti

tle and URL, which the page also controls.
[该节后续省略]
